text:
ashley: Heads up - saw a correlated spike in ECC errors + Xid bursts in us-west-2 around 03:14 UTC, and a couple of pods timed out during KV cache warmup. Not full outage but noisy.

miguel: Can you paste the short graph? sounds like the usual flaky card pattern but the ECC+Xid correlation matters.

ashley: small snapshot: `ecc_rate ~ 12/min`, `xid_err ~ 45 spikes/min` across 3 nodes. GPU temps fine. Also noticed Slurm jobs on those nodes had extra retries.

vivian: Are these on Dedicated or Private clusters? capacity/scheduling differs.

ashley: Dedicated pool (reserved) in us-west-2. We still have free capacity in us-east-1 but cross-region failover is costly and increases latency for some customers.

leo: Suggest we tune the auto-cordon sensitivity to require two signals (Xid spike + ECC threshold) within a 2m window before immediate drain. Single-signal should just soft-taint and increase probing frequency.

monitoring-bot: alert triggered: gpu_xid_burst_count > 30 for 120s on node gpu-node-22; gpu_ecc_uncorrected > 10 for 120s on node gpu-node-22

tony: +1 to 2-signal debounce. Also prefer a cost-aware evacuation policy: if region spare capacity < 10%, delay full eviction and perform partial job migration (preempt low-priority) instead of draining immediately.

ashley: Trying to capture that in a quick scoring rule. Proposal: node_score = w1*ecc_norm + w2*xid_norm + w3*temp_norm + w4*(1 - region_spare_ratio). If score > 0.8 -> cordon+drain; if 0.5-0.8 -> soft-taint + increase monitors.

miguel: Can we express that as a Prometheus alert + orchestration policy? We need an alert that only fires the high-severity webhook when both signals co-occur and region_spare_ratio < 0.1.

vivian: Also remember k8s vs Slurm semantics: k8s drain can respect pod disruption budgets; Slurm eviction is job-level. We should avoid killing long-running Slurm jobs if we can migrate their GPUs with node-level GPU isolation first.

ashley: Draft alert rule (very rough):
```
ALERT GPUMultiSignalHigh
IF (sum_over_time(gpu_xid_bursts[2m]) > 30) and (sum_over_time(gpu_ecc_uncorrected[2m]) > 8)
AND on(node) (region_spare_capacity_ratio{region=\"us-west-2\"} < 0.10)
FOR 1m
LABELS { severity=\"page\" }
ANNOTATIONS { runbook=\"infra/sre/gpu-multisignal-failover\" }
```

leo: Nice. For orchestration, propose 2-step webhook: first -> /api/v1/autocordon with body {node, score, action:\"soft-taint\"} then if score persists 10m -> action:\"drain\". Keep the webhook idempotent.

tony: For Slurm, instead of hard cancel we can `scontrol update NodeName=... State=DRAIN Reason=\"gpu-multi-signal-probable\"` which prevents new jobs and lets admins decide migration. Add SLO-aware cutoff to auto-cancel only <2h jobs.

infra-sre: Concern: risk of oscillation when Xid bursts are very short. Add rate-limiter: only allow 1 auto-drain per-node per 6h, and keep a cooldown that prefers manual review after 2 events in 12h.

ashley: Agree. Also suggest a short live-check job that runs `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC, Xid` and grabs bottom-up logs; attach to the incident when webhook triggers so oncall has context.

miguel: Implementation checklist:
- update Prom rule with region-aware label
- webhook payload includes recent metrics window + suggested action
- implement soft-taint endpoint + idempotent drain endpoint
- Slurm handler respects job-length SLOs
- add cooldown / rate limit and rollback path

vivian: We should also add a cost-estimate field in the webhook: estimated_cross_region_cost_usd to help SRE decide auto vs manual.

leo: Quick config sketch for webhook payload (pseudo):
```
{ \"node\":\"gpu-node-22\", \"score\":\"0.83\", \"signals\":[\"xid\",\"ecc\"], \"region\":\"us-west-2\", \"region_spare\":0.06, \"estimated_cross_region_cost_usd\":\"12.40\" }
```

ashley: Testing plan: simulate spike on a single node in staging with 1) single signal, 2) both signals + high spare, 3) both signals + low spare. Validate soft-taint -> drain sequence + Slurm behavior.

tony: When you run the staging test, include a runbook step to check `dmesg | tail` and NV bug list; sometimes Xid bursts are NV kernel that recovers after soft-reset and doesn't need replacement.

ashley: Will run tests tomorrow morning. Putting the runbook link: /runbooks/gpu-multi-signal-failover

miguel: Thanks, please post results in this thread and tag @infra-sre. :white_check_mark:

ashley: Will do. Starting a heatmap export now and scheduling the staging sim for 09:00 PST.

monitoring-bot: incident created: gpu-multi-1997654321, assigned to infra-sre

leo: One last ask: surface the local job priority vector so the policy can preempt best-effort jobs first. Otherwise we might evict expensive paid workloads by mistake.

ashley: Added to checklist. I'll share the test logs when done.

miguel: Nice plan. If the tests look good we can roll a small canary to 5% of nodes in us-west-2 next week.

vivian: +1 to canary. Also add metric for false-positive rate so product teams can see customer impact.

ashley: copying checklist into the PR for the orchestrator. thanks everyone.
